messages.content: You and the same partner repeatedly make your decisions simultaneously. The partner also receives a fresh 20 yen and can give it to you under the same doubling rule. For this interaction your payoff is 40 yen if both give, 0 if you give and the partner keeps, 60 if you keep and the partner gives, and 20 if both keep. The partner's payoff is respectively 40, 60, 0, 20. You do not see the partner's current choice before deciding. displayed_other_report concerns this same partner's previous decision. Pseudonyms stay fixed, so this is the same partner throughout. Predict the participant's actual give-or-keep decision. You receive a fresh endowment of 20 Japanese yen for this decision. GIVE_20_YEN means give all 20 yen: you lose this endowment and the recipient receives 40 yen because it is doubled. KEEP_20_YEN means do not give: you retain the 20 yen and that transfer gives the recipient nothing. There is no partial transfer. Total money earned during the experiment is paid individually at the end. Decisions are anonymous and screens are separated by partitions. Information about another person's action is sometimes transmitted incorrectly in either direction; the displayed report is what you were told and need not equal that person's actual action. No numerical error rate is disclosed. A null report means no report is supplied for this decision, not a report of not giving. displayed_own_previous_action is your own last choice shown on screen, or null before any own choice. Own prior history entries are [own decision number, other-person report available BEFORE that past choice, your past choice]; these entries do not include feedback learned after the current choice. No individual age or sex is retained in these records. Output only GIVE_20_YEN or KEEP_20_YEN without explanation.

That upstream donor is a different person from your downstream recipient; you cannot immediately interact with the person with whom you last interacted. displayed_other_report concerns that upstream donor's action toward you. Your current choice is relayed to your downstream recipient, who then decides for another person. Multiple chains proceed concurrently, so consecutive own decisions may occur in different chains. Fresh random three-letter pseudonyms are used for every decision and never reused, preventing identification of recurring people. Exact pseudonyms and chain membership were not retained; do not infer identities from past entries. Your giving loses 20 yen and benefits the downstream person by 40 yen, while any incoming gift is separate. Predict the participant's actual give-or-keep decision. KEEP_20_YEN means do not give: you retain the 20 yen and that transfer gives the recipient nothing. There is no partial transfer. Total money earned during the experiment is paid individually at the end. Decisions are anonymous and screens are separated by partitions. Information about another person's action is sometimes transmitted incorrectly in either direction; the displayed report is what you were told and need not equal that person's actual action. No numerical error rate is disclosed. A null report means no report is supplied for this decision, not a report of not giving. displayed_own_previous_action is your own last choice shown on screen, or null before any own choice. Own prior history entries are [own decision number, other-person report available BEFORE that past choice, your past choice]; these entries do not include feedback learned after the current choice. That upstream donor is a different person from your downstream recipient; you cannot immediately interact with the person with whom you last interacted. displayed_other_report concerns that upstream donor's action toward you. Fresh random three-letter pseudonyms are used for every decision and never reused, preventing identification of recurring people. Exact pseudonyms and chain membership were not retained; do not infer identities from past entries. Your giving loses 20 yen and benefits the downstream person by 40 yen, while any incoming gift is separate. Predict the participant's actual give-or-keep decision. KEEP_20_YEN means do not give: you retain the 20 yen and that transfer gives the recipient nothing. There is no partial transfer. Total money earned during the experiment is paid individually at the end. Decisions are anonymous and screens are separated by partitions. Information about another person's action is sometimes transmitted incorrectly in either direction; the displayed report is what you were told and need not equal that person's actual action. No numerical error rate is disclosed. A null report means no report is supplied for this decision, not a report of not giving. displayed_own_previous_action is your own last choice shown on screen, or null before any own choice. Own prior history entries are [own decision number, other-person report available BEFORE that past choice, your past choice]; these entries do not include feedback learned after the current choice. Fresh random three-letter pseudonyms are used for every decision and never reused, preventing identification of recurring people. Information about another person's action is sometimes transmitted incorrectly in either direction; the displayed report is what you were told and need not equal that person's actual action. No numerical error rate is disclosed. A null report means no report is supplied for this decision, not a report of not giving. displayed_own_previous_action is your own last choice shown on screen, or null before any own choice.
